A1.justification: Despite the changed title and organization, both PDFs describe the same BP/FMAD/ZO comparison. Their complete main texts and appendices provide readable, matchable experimental and theoretical material.

before.justification: V1 reports original accuracy, convergence, memory, and computational-cost experiments, including benchmark comparisons and appendix sensitivity and failure-mode analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds synthetic regression, full fine-tuning, SignZO comparisons, and further diagnostic experiments.

M1.justification: The gradient estimators and proposed accumulation and adaptive-perturbation procedures remain unchanged. Custom layerwise jvp propagation implements the existing FMAD computation; SignZO and alternative sampling configurations are additional comparisons and ablations.

E1.justification: The seven language and visual-question-answering datasets are retained. Section 4.6 adds synthetic linear regression, a distinct but limited addition to task coverage. Additional dataset-model combinations otherwise reuse existing tasks.

E2.justification: SignZO is newly evaluated in Table 16 and Figure 15. Figure 13 extends the optimizer comparison with FMAD-MULTIPLE and FMAD-ACCUMULATE. Conversely, v2 Table 4 omits FMAD-ACCUMULATE from the AGNews compute comparison in v1 Table 3, although it remains elsewhere.

E3.justification: New protocols include the controlled MLP regression experiment, an OPT-13B LoRA sweep through rank 128 and full fine-tuning, and perturbation-distribution and normalization controls. The reported ZO BoolQ learning rate also changes from 10^-4 in v1 Table 6 to 10^-3 in v2 Table 8; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds implementation-overhead controls, gradient-norm trajectories, higher-rank/full-fine-tuning sensitivity, and optimizer diagnostics for accumulation and multiple perturbations. Appendices E.7 and E.9 additionally examine distribution normalization and OPT-13B perturbation budgets. The earlier optimizer and SVRG analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report three runs with seeds 0, 1, and 2 and the same steady-state accuracy averaging and variance procedure. V1 Table 8 is retained as v2 Table 10, without a new uncertainty-reporting practice or statistical test.

E6.justification: The main accuracy table changes only by rounding, but substantial new results appear. V2 Table 15 reports full-fine-tuning accuracies of 96.68% for BP and 32.37% for ZO, with FMAD producing NaNs; Table 16 reports 82.6% for SignZO versus 73.6% for ZO. New MLP, runtime, and diagnostic results are added, while the earlier AGNews FMAD-ACCUMULATE compute row disappears.

T1.justification: The original convergence lemmas and proofs remain in the renumbered Appendix H. V2 adds Corollary H.10 on parameter choices for a claimed O(d/T) ZO rate and Corollary H.11 defining ADAM amplification and proposing a corresponding convergence bound and proof. These extend the theoretical substance beyond relocation.

C1.justification: The headline BP advantages and numerical contribution claims remain. V2 more explicitly limits the recommendation to LLM training and fine-tuning, emphasizes correcting incomplete benchmarking, and presents the theoretical contribution more as a common-framework synthesis than as filling a previously missing theoretical foundation.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations attributing FMAD inefficiency primarily to the algorithm, explaining how averaging mitigates ADAM instability, and explaining normalization-related accuracy losses. It also discusses theoretical versus practical learning rates and makes a stronger extrapolation from low-rank failures to full fine-tuning. The unchanged limitations section still describes full fine-tuning as future work despite the new results.

D1.justification: V2 supplies MLP parameter count, split, optimizer and learning rate, custom jvp implementation information, explicit batch-specific timings, and SignZO update details. The advertised code repository changes from The_Cost_of_Avoiding_Backpropagation to Gradient_Estimation_Methods. Most existing implementation and hyperparameter documentation is retained.

R1.justification: New Table 1 positions prior methods by their evaluation coverage. Related work adds HIZOO and biological-plausibility discussions, with additional LoRA and checkpointing references elsewhere. These extend the existing positioning around incomplete efficiency comparisons; most prior-work discussion remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and theoretical overview are substantially rewritten. Main-text theorem statements give way to a shorter comparative overview, dedicated implementation and failure-analysis sections are introduced, and the broader-impact statement moves out of the appendices. Appendix organization and cross-references are extensively revised.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column format to a two-column conference layout, with resized and relocated displays and vertically rearranged Figure 2 panels. V2 adds literature, MLP, runtime, full-fine-tuning, and SignZO tables plus several diagnostic plots; Figure 13 combines retained traces with new ones.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses v1's LoRA-only evidence gap and adds useful implementation and stability controls. However, the new theoretical support has substantive gaps: Corollary H.10 retains a T^-1/2 remainder while claiming O(d/T), and H.11 substitutes a lower error bound into an upper-bound argument. Section 4.6 also gives inconsistent descriptions of convergence MSE. Broader evidence and new reliability problems coexist, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
